From 9709b56d908acc120fe8b4ae250b3c9d749ea832 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Alexander Koskovich <akoskovich@pm.me>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 18:43:47 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] net: ipa: fix GENERIC_CMD register field masks for IPA v5.0+

Fix the field masks to match the hardware layout documented in
downstream GSI (GSI_V3_0_EE_n_GSI_EE_GENERIC_CMD_*).

Notably this fixes a WARN I was seeing when I tried to send "stop"
to the MPSS remoteproc while IPA was up.

Fixes: faf0678ec8a0 ("net: ipa: add IPA v5.0 GSI register definitions")
Signed-off-by: Alexander Koskovich <akoskovich@pm.me>
Signed-off-by: Luca Weiss <luca.weiss@fairphone.com>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260403-milos-ipa-v1-1-01e9e4e03d3e@fairphone.com
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ipa/reg/gsi_reg-v5.0.c b/drivers/net/ipa/reg/gsi_reg-v5.0.c
index 36d1e65df71b..3334d8e20ad2 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ipa/reg/gsi_reg-v5.0.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ipa/reg/gsi_reg-v5.0.c
@@ -156,9 +156,10 @@ REG_FIELDS(EV_CH_CMD, ev_ch_cmd, 0x00025010 + 0x12000 * GSI_EE_AP);
 
 static const u32 reg_generic_cmd_fmask[] = {
 	[GENERIC_OPCODE]				= GENMASK(4, 0),
-	[GENERIC_CHID]					= GENMASK(9, 5),
-	[GENERIC_EE]					= GENMASK(13, 10),
-						/* Bits 14-31 reserved */
+	[GENERIC_CHID]					= GENMASK(12, 5),
+	[GENERIC_EE]					= GENMASK(16, 13),
+						/* Bits 17-23 reserved */
+	[GENERIC_PARAMS]				= GENMASK(31, 24),
 };
 
 REG_FIELDS(GENERIC_CMD, generic_cmd, 0x00025018 + 0x12000 * GSI_EE_AP);
-- 
2.34.1

**Summary of modifications:**

**File: `drivers/net/ipa/reg/gsi_reg-v5.0.c`**

- Updated the field masks for the `GENERIC_CMD` register:
  - `GENERIC_CHID` changed from `GENMASK(9, 5)` to `GENMASK(12, 5)`.
  - `GENERIC_EE` changed from `GENMASK(13, 10)` to `GENMASK(16, 13)`.
  - Added a new field `GENERIC_PARAMS` with mask `GENMASK(31, 24)`, replacing the previously reserved bits (14‑31).
- Reserved bits description updated to “Bits 17‑23 reserved”.

**Relationships:**

- This is the only file modified. The corrections align the register bit‑field definitions with the hardware specification, fixing a bug that caused a WARN when stopping the MPSS remoteproc while the IPA driver was active. No cross‑file dependencies exist.

Here is the commit message:
net: ipa: fix GENERIC_CMD register field masks for IPA v5.0+

Fix the field masks to match the hardware layout documented in
downstream GSI (GSI_V3_0_EE_n_GSI_EE_GENERIC_CMD_*).

Notably this fixes a WARN I was seeing when I tried to send "stop"
to the MPSS remoteproc while IPA was up.

Fixes: faf0678ec8a0 ("net: ipa: add IPA v5.0 GSI register definitions")
Signed-off-by: Alexander Koskovich <akoskovich@pm.me>
Signed-off-by: Luca Weiss <luca.weiss@fairphone.com>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260403-milos-ipa-v1-1-01e9e4e03d3e@fairphone.com
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

Here is the root cause:
The field masks for the GENERIC_CMD register in IPA v5.0+ were incorrectly defined, causing misprogramming when sending commands (e.g., stop) to the MPSS remoteproc while IPA was up, which triggered a WARN.

Here is the patch:
 static const u32 reg_generic_cmd_fmask[] = {
 	[GENERIC_OPCODE]				= GENMASK(4, 0),
-	[GENERIC_CHID]					= GENMASK(9, 5),
-	[GENERIC_EE]					= GENMASK(13, 10),
-						/* Bits 14-31 reserved */
+	[GENERIC_CHID]					= GENMASK(12, 5),
+	[GENERIC_EE]					= GENMASK(16, 13),
+						/* Bits 17-23 reserved */
+	[GENERIC_PARAMS]				= GENMASK(31, 24),
 };

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
[GENERIC_CHID]					= GENMASK(9, 5),
[GENERIC_EE]					= GENMASK(13, 10),
						/* Bits 14-31 reserved */
Reason:
These field masks do not match the hardware layout for IPA v5.0+, causing the GENERIC_CMD register to be programmed with incorrect bit positions for channel ID (CHID) and execution environment (EE). When sending a "stop" command to the MPSS remoteproc, the misprogrammed fields lead to a WARN trigger because the command is not correctly formatted or targets the wrong parameters.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
[GENERIC_CHID]					= GENMASK(12, 5),
[GENERIC_EE]					= GENMASK(16, 13),
[GENERIC_PARAMS]				= GENMASK(31, 24),
Reason:
The corrected masks align with the hardware documentation (GSI_V3_0_EE_n_GSI_EE_GENERIC_CMD_*). They correctly define the bit ranges for CHID, EE, and add the missing PARAMS field. This ensures commands like "stop" are properly encoded, avoiding the WARN and enabling correct operation with the MPSS remoteproc.
